sights.w: Opened in 2001 as the first Universal Studios park in Asia; one of Japan's most visited theme parks, with areas including The Wizarding World of Harry Potter and Super Nintendo World.

sights.address: 1-1-10 Kaigan-dori, Minato-ku, Osaka (Tempozan Harbor Village), Japan
sights.w: One of Japan's largest aquariums, built around a 5,400-ton central Pacific tank holding a whale shark, with exhibits themed on the Pacific Rim.

sights.address: Tempozan Harbor Village, 1-1-10 Kaigan-dori, Minato-ku, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: A 112.5 m Ferris wheel beside Kaiyūkan in Tempozan Harbor Village, with a roughly 15-minute ride over Osaka Bay and the city skyline.

sights.address: Osaka Prefectural Government Sakishima Building, 1-14-16 Nanko-kita, Suminoe-ku, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: Observation deck 252 m up atop the Sakishima building (completed 1995), giving a 360-degree panorama of Osaka Bay; known for night views.
Head shrine of over two thousand Sumiyoshi shrines across Japan, protecting travellers and sailors; its four main halls face west in the ancient Sumiyoshi-zukuri style.

sights.n: Mozu Kofun Group — Daisen Kofun (Emperor Nintoku's Tomb)
sights.w: Cluster of 5th-century keyhole tombs in Sakai, UNESCO World Heritage (2019) with the Furuichi group; Daisen Kofun, attributed to Emperor Nintoku, is the largest grave in the world by area (~840 m with moats). The mound itself is off-limits.

sights.address: Daisen Park, Mozusekiun-cho, Sakai-ku, Sakai, Osaka, Japan
sights.w: Museum in Daisen Park tracing the history of the port town of Sakai, starting with the kofun tombs and artifacts excavated from them.

sights.n: Sakai Plaza of Rikyū and Akiko (Sakai Rishō no Mori)
sights.w: Cultural facility opened in 2015 on Sen no Rikyū and poet Yosano Akiko, with a tea-ceremony museum, tea experiences and Sakai Taian, a reproduction of the National Treasure Taian tea room.

sights.n: Expo '70 Commemorative Park & Tower of the Sun
sights.w: Vast park on the grounds of the 1970 Japan World Exposition, the first in Asia; Tarō Okamoto's 70 m Tower of the Sun stands over the main entrance as its icon.
Forested valley just north of Osaka with a roughly 3 km riverside trail from Hankyu Minoo Station to the 33 m Minoo Waterfall; famous for autumn colours.
Mountain temple above Minoh known as the temple of victory, its grounds dotted with thousands of small red daruma dolls left by wishers.
